parts.text:
2
Which unit is not equivalent to a unit of energy?
A
N m
B
V C
C
W s
D
kg m s–2

hints: Start from the SI unit of energy, the joule $\text{J}$, and test each of $\text{N m}$, $\text{V C}$ and $\text{W s}$ against a definition of work or energy.
Link each product to energy using $W = Fd$, $W = VQ$ and $W = Pt$, where $F$ is force, $Q$ is charge and $P$ is power.
Expand $\text{kg m s}^{-2}$ as mass times acceleration using $F = ma$ and ask what extra $\text{m}$ would be needed to make $\text{kg m}^{2}\text{s}^{-2}$ for energy.
walkthrough: Recall the SI unit of energy is the joule, $\text{J}$, which in base units is $\text{kg m}^{2}\text{s}^{-2}$.
Check $\text{N m}$ using work $W = Fd$: newton times metre is force times distance, so $1 \text{ N m} = 1 \text{ J}$.
Check $\text{V C}$ using $V = W/Q$ rearranged to $W = VQ$: volt times coulomb is $(\text{J C}^{-1}) \times \text{C} = \text{J}$.
Check $\text{W s}$ using $P = W/t$ rearranged to $W = Pt$: watt times second is $(\text{J s}^{-1}) \times \text{s} = \text{J}$.
Check $\text{kg m s}^{-2}$ using $F = ma$: $\text{kg} \times \text{m s}^{-2}$ equals one newton $\text{N}$, which is force and lacks the second metre needed for $\text{N m}$. This is option D.

A.explanation: From $W = Fd$, $\text{N m}$ is force times distance, which is the joule $\text{J}$, a unit of energy.

B.explanation: From $V = W/Q$, $W = VQ$, so $\text{V C}$ is joule $\text{J}$, a unit of electrical energy.

C.explanation: From $P = W/t$, $W = Pt$, so $\text{W s}$ is joule $\text{J}$, a unit of energy.

D.explanation: Since $F = ma$, $\text{kg m s}^{-2}$ is the newton $\text{N}$, the unit of force, not energy.
